name: Nod
description: An open-source personal assistant from n8n. Runs on your computer, talks to you on Telegram, browses, schedules and works across your apps, with your own model and keys.
description_good_justification: The README and https://nod.n8n.io/ say what Nod is: an open-source personal assistant that runs on your computer with its own workspace and browser, works across your apps and asks before acting.
interact_justification: The README links the docs, releases, GitHub Discussions, Discord and the n8n community forum. CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to report bugs, ask questions and send pull requests: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull request template list the required checks, the test policy, the PR title format and the data rules: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is approved by the Open Source Initiative.
documentation_basics_justification: https://nod.n8n.io/docs/ covers installing, using, connecting apps, configuring and deploying Nod.
documentation_interface_justification: Configuration reference: https://nod.n8n.io/docs/deploy/configuration/ . How the system works: https://nod.n8n.io/docs/how-it-works/architecture/
sites_https_justification: The homepage and docs (https://nod.n8n.io), the repository and the release downloads (github.com) are served over HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and Discussions, which are searchable, addressable by URL and need no proprietary client: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/discussions
english_justification: All documentation and discussion is in English, and English bug reports and questions are accepted.
maintained_justification: Nod is developed by n8n, with commits most days and regular releases.
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when.
repo_interim_justification: Work between releases lands on main through public pull requests.
version_unique_justification: Each release has its own version and tag, such as nod-v0.6.0.
version_semver_justification: Releases use Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH), derived from Conventional Commit titles.
version_tags_justification: Every release is a git tag nod-vX.Y.Z: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/tags
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/releases lists the features and fixes in each release, with links to their pull requests.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability with a CVE or similar assignment yet. Confirmed vulnerabilities get a GitHub security advisory and are named in the release notes, as SECURITY.md says: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/security/policy
report_responses_justification: The team triages every bug report from GitHub Issues and in-app feedback. The repository became public on 10 November 2026.
enhancement_responses_justification: The team responds to enhancement requests in GitHub Issues and Discussions.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/security/advisories/new , or n8n's Vulnerability Disclosure Program, both described in https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/security/policy
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging a report within 3 business days and sharing a first assessment within 10.
build_justification: pnpm run build builds the server and web app; pnpm run desktop:build builds the desktop app. See CONTRIBUTING.md.
build_floss_tools_justification: Node.js, pnpm, TypeScript, Vite, Electron and Docker are all FLOSS.
test_justification: pnpm test runs the deterministic tests and pnpm run test:integration runs every test in Linux with a disposable PostgreSQL and Chromium: https://nod.n8n.io/docs/contribute/checks-and-tests/
test_invocation_justification: pnpm test and pnpm run test:integration.
test_most_justification: Coverage is not a gate. Tests target the core harness, sandbox isolation, safety, owner isolation and real integration contracts, per the test policy: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/AGENTS.md#tests
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the checks, tests and build on every pull request and push to main, and they are required to merge.
test_policy_justification: The test policy requires tests that would catch a real regression for new behaviour in the core harness, sandbox isolation, safety, owner isolation and integration contracts: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/AGENTS.md#tests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent behaviour changes in those areas land with tests, and the pull request template asks for them.
tests_documented_added_justification: The pull request template asks whether new tests would catch a real regression, linking the test policy: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/.github/pull_request_template.md
warnings_justification: TypeScript runs in strict mode (tsc --noEmit) with an architecture check, as part of pnpm run check on every pull request.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any type error or failed check, so main has none outstanding.
know_secure_design_justification: Nod is built around explicit safety rules: one trust check for every outside action, private Vault entry that never shows secrets to the model, a sandboxed workspace without keys, and owner isolation. https://nod.n8n.io/docs/trust/
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainers handle common vulnerability classes with structural guards: public-address URL checks against SSRF, sandboxed file previews against XSS, owner-key local access, secret redaction and no secrets in the sandbox. The code had security audits before going public.
crypto_published_justification: Only published algorithms are used: AES-256-GCM, SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-256.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptography goes through Node.js crypto (OpenSSL). Nod implements no cryptographic primitives of its own.
crypto_floss_justification: Node.js crypto and OpenSSL are FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: 256-bit AES keys and 256-bit HMAC keys; TLS uses Node.js and Chromium defaults.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithms (MD4, MD5, single DES, RC4, Dual_EC_DRBG) are used.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: SHA-1 appears only where an outside format requires it: HMAC-SHA1 for authenticator codes when a website's key specifies it (RFC 6238), and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 to read Chrome's macOS cookie store format.
crypto_pfs_justification: Connections use TLS through Node.js and Chromium defaults, which negotiate ECDHE key exchange.
crypto_password_storage_justification: Nod does not authenticate users with passwords; local access uses a random owner access key. Saved website logins must be reused, so they are encrypted with AES-256-GCM rather than hashed.
crypto_random_justification: Keys, nonces and tokens come from crypto.randomBytes, crypto.randomUUID or crypto.getRandomValues.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases and updates download over HTTPS from GitHub Releases. Mac builds are signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized; Windows builds are signed by n8n GmbH.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are fetched over HTTP; every download uses HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Dependabot alerts and security updates are on, with no open alerts.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Dependabot security updates open fixes automatically, and the team merges them quickly.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks scans every pull request and push. GitHub secret scanning and push protection are on and found no secrets in the full history.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (JavaScript/TypeScript and Python) and Semgrep run on every pull request and push to main: https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/.github/workflows/security.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security queries and Semgrep's p/ci rules look for common vulnerabilities.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Every CodeQL alert is triaged, and none are open.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and push to main, and weekly.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzer or dedicated dynamic analysis tool yet; the integration tests run the real server against PostgreSQL and Chromium.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Nod is written in TypeScript and JavaScript, which are memory-safe.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The test suites run with Node.js assertions enabled.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is used beyond the test suites.
